notes.title: I remembered my password
notes.content:
[p]Jokes aside, I’m here with this announcement, after a [b]loong[/b] time without any updates, to inform you that the update I’ve been working on for the past few [b]months[/b] is now in the [b]final stages[/b]. Since this is a significant update, as it will be the one that takes the game [b]out of early access[/b], I’m making sure there are as few issues as possible. If needed, small updates will be made to address any potential issues. I should highlight that I do everything [b]myself[/b], so the [b]implementation and testing[/b], depending on the [b]complexity[/b] of what I’m working on, might influence how long it will take to finish. [b]Enough with the excuses[/b], let’s get to the important stuff:[/p][p][b]
Missions
[/b]The game will now have a light narrative approach, with [b]objectives[/b] that, once completed, will [b]unlock new things[/b] (nothing too complex, but different).[/p][p][b]
Balancing[/b]
I’ve been pretty negligent with the game’s balancing because I was always focused on adding something new, and didn’t have time to properly address this. Balancing is a crucial stage, as it's where you define the game's difficulty curve. At launch, when I first released the game, players died extremely quickly because enemies spawned too fast and shot almost without delay, which made the game frustrating to deal with (not to mention other bugs that literally broke the game, causing players to lose their current progress). Since the launch, I’ve done numerous updates, each aiming to improve the difficulty and the sense of progression that items/cards bring to the player. [b]Player feedback[/b] [b]is essential[/b] at this stage, because [b]if I mess up[/b] something and you feel I did, I’ll definitely [b]re-evaluate[/b] the situation.[/p][p][b]
Fixes[/b]
Numerous bug fixes (both visual and code-related), involving both keyboard and controller. I will list each change individually in the update 1.0 post, as there are quite a lot.[/p][p][b]
Deadlines[/b]
I can’t give an exact date yet, as I’m reviewing [b]every[/b] aspect of the game, but sometime in [b]September[/b] seems like a good guess. Thanks for your patience.[/p]

notes.title: Good News!
Goals
notes.content:
We reached the mark of [b]100 copies[/b] sold. Seriously, I didn't expect this number so soon and especially in early access. [b]Thank you very much[/b] to everyone who gave the game a chance even though it still needs polish and content. Since the game's launch, significant improvements have been made to gameplay as well as more content and functions for things already included in the game, such as effects on accessories. But I know that I still have to say with conviction that the game is in the state I planned.

This end of the year is a time of great content and polish for the game, but also many unforeseen events. It wasn't my intention, but the story update planned for this December will have to be [b]postponed[/b]. Some things are beyond my reach, such as art. We had unforeseen events in this part and also due to the dialogue system and new questlines. Everything that has been worked on in the last few months has been new learning for me and it has been a great challenge to complete each stage, one step at a time.

Each review, comment and new player is a [b]wonderful achievement[/b] that I intend to repay with a game that is closest to everyone's liking. 

[b]Without further ado, I would like to wish a belated Merry Christmas and a prosperous New Year to everyone. [/b]

notes.title: Slowly but steadily
notes.content:
Yes, I'm still [b]alive[/b] and working on the game. In the meantime I've been testing the new mission system I'm creating to tell the game's narrative to have a starting point and a consistent conclusion. [b]Don't expect[/b] a great story or create high expectations, but I will do my best to at least be tolerable from beginning to end. As they are fixed missions with fixed objectives, as soon as the player finishes the story mode [b]I intend to add a new mechanic/resource[/b] where the missions are carried out. I'm still thinking about the possibilities but I think will end up being a [b]special store[/b]. I'll give more details when I'm actually working on this feature.

[b]Happy gaming everyone![/b]

notes.title: PATCH 0.4.0
notes.content:
Yes, it took a little longer than expected, but it's finally here. [b]LAST MINI BOSS COMPLETED[/b]. With this major stage completed, I can now focus on the final stretch of the game, which involves alternative game modes, a mission system for the main story, and a final final boss, among others. The [b]"Informal Roadmap"[/b] that I mentioned in the last post will be explained in a simple and direct way: goals.

Now that I've managed to finish the last mini boss of the initial gameplay loop, I can calmly focus on the next stages, which will probably take longer to complete, namely:

[b]MAIN STORY[/b]

It will be based on a mission system. It will be used exclusively to conclude the game's narrative. The player will have fixed objectives that they will have to complete during their game in order to unlock the main story route. The game's Final Boss will be completed together with the release of the story mode missions. Once the player finishes this part, there will be additional content in the location used to complete these missions.

[b]OPTIMIZATION[/b]

I am aware of [b]performance issues[/b] that we have encountered in the current state of the game, and so I intend to do a general review of the code for the entire combat part to identify the cause and make the game as optimized as possible. Better optimization means that a wider audience can enjoy the game, including players on portable devices such as the [b]Steam Deck[/b]. As it stands at the moment, it runs with extremely fluctuating performance, hence my emphasis on this optimization part.

[b]NEW GAME MODES[/b]

- New game modes. Considered so far, in addition to the current one of going to wave 100:

- Infinite Mode;
- Hardcore Mode;
- Darkness Mode;

The new game modes will be added as additional [b]after[/b] the completion of other game priorities.

I won't give dates so as not to commit to deadlines I can't meet, but my goal is to at least have the main story completed by the [b]end of December[/b]. I might finish it sooner, or I might finish it later. But I'll do my best to meet my estimate.

notes.title: Last Mini Boss arriving
notes.content:
started this week creating the mechanics for the game's last mini boss. Once this is done, there will be[b] 3 possible bosses[/b] that the player will encounter in their matches until wave 100, where the match ends. More details on the next update will be made as soon as the update with the mini boss is published. I'm already thinking about how I'm going to approach the mission system of the [b]main story[/b] that I mentioned. What I can say is that it has something to do with that [b]door[/b] that no one can use before facing the mini bosses ːdemoneyeːːdemoneyeː

The next update with the mini boss is scheduled for [b]next week[/b] with the same reason as the previous one: I need to [b]implement, test, validate and then refine[/b]. More time means less chance of bugs and glitches that would take away any possible fun experience for the player. 

The game is in version [b]0.3.0[/b], which means that the next update with the arrival of the last mini boss will become [b]0.4.0[/b]. The next content updates may, or may not, add more value to the game version as a way to see how close it is to the final version [b]1.0.0[/b], but I will never use it as an excuse just to finish the game. game before delivering less. In the next update I will give more details about this final stretch that I am planning and possible delivery time estimates for each thing. Almost like a [b]ROADMAP[/b], but informal. I thank everyone who believes in the project.

notes.title: UPDATE - 0.3.0
notes.content:
"Wait, shouldn't this be version 0.2.4?" Yes and no. (more yes than no). [b]I'll explain everything at the end of this post[/b] if you're interested. But first...

I worked like crazy to bring this new addition to the game as quickly as possible and with as few issues as possible...


[b]NEW BOSS[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44843544/807a1c7f911da54443d63b184665d9ebfa51bdfa.png[/img]


Don't expect too much complexity in its mechanics, but I guarantee it will be more engaging than the only mini-boss that has been available until now. With a bigger variety, my intention of making the gameplay more random is coming to life. Instead of always facing the same boss, you might encounter a different one. That sense of not having control over certain aspects of the game is what fascinates me the most in this genre, and executing it in a fun way is my biggest goal. From concept to execution, the mechanics of this boss took me about 2 weeks, requiring more time for full implementation.

The next planned content will be: Hardcore Difficulty (if you thought it was hard already, get ready) and a new mini-boss. I’m not sure about the order of implementation, but this will definitely be my next focus. 

Now for the explanation:

Since this is my first project, I don’t have much experience or knowledge about how to properly catalog the game's versions, so I opted for a simpler format to understand. Smaller updates will increase the version by 0.0.1, while significant changes will jump by 0.1.0 (hence the leap to 0.3.0). Since this is a “new” version, I decided to register it as 0.3.0 instead of 0.2.4, as I believe the changes warrant a version jump.

All past and future updates serve both for me (as the developer) and for players or future players, allowing them to follow the game's development progress in detail if they're interested. Honestly, it helps me a lot to stay focused. My plan is to bump the version by 0.1.0 whenever something significant is added, such as additional content or a new game mode. The goal is to follow this pattern until I reach the long-awaited version 1.0.0 (the official release), where I’ll have successfully completed the game and made it as polished as possible.

Note: I’ll be taking [b]a week[/b] off after these intense weeks to return at full strength, but any urgent bug or glitch fixes will still be implemented if needed.

notes.title: Next boss approaches
notes.content: I had unexpected issues with the new mechanics of the next mini boss. Therefore, I will postpone this update until the middle/end of next week to remove all possible glitches/bugs.

notes.title: PATCH - 0.2.3
PATCH - 0.2.3
Future ideas and plans
notes.content:
With many structural issues being resolved, we are getting closer to the point where additional content updates will be added to the game. Mechanics like accessory effects or card rerolls don't count as additional content to me, so I want to emphasize what will be added in the long term from now on. The goals I will mention here won’t necessarily be implemented in this order, but they will definitely be implemented over time.

[b]3 NEW MINI BOSSES[/b]

Each with a different combat mechanic. Currently, there is only one mini-boss, which can make the game monotonous and predictable over time. By adding more mini-bosses, not only will there be more content, but it will also enhance the randomness factor I want to bring to the game.

Adding 2 More Game Modes: Endless and Shadow Mode (Name May Change)

[b]SHADOW MODE[/b]

As the name suggests, this will be a dark game mode, where the main sources of light will be enemy projectiles, your own projectiles, and torches in the environment. I've been working on this occasionally to see if it's feasible, and it seems like it is, so I’d like to list it here as a possible future game mode.

[b]ENDLESS MODE[/b]

The current game mode has the objective of reaching wave 100, and the player is rewarded for making it to the end. In this mode, there will be no wave limits, and scaling will be continuous. It will be a mode entirely focused on challenging yourself to see how far you can go. For this mode to work, more adjustments will need to be made to the game’s scaling and enemy spawn times, as I’ve noticed that spawn times are too short at the beginning, making the gameplay too slow initially and only moderate at the end.

[b]STORY MODE[/b]

This was the main focus from the beginning, but due to my technical limitations, it had to be put on the back burner, leaving only the current game mode that goes up to wave 100. The way I’m considering implementing this is by having missions assigned by Riggs in the lobby, and the player will need to complete objectives within the game to fulfill the mission. Once the player completes the objective, they will be able to access a certain door in the gameplay that will advance the main storyline.

[b]MORE CARDS[/b]

This is an essential part of a roguelite game, right? Currently, the game has 27 cards (13 of which are specific to staves), which can be a low number considering the repetitive gameplay nature of the game. I'm working on new cards that will have dual effects (e.g., "increase x, decrease y") to make for a riskier but more impactful trade-off in the player's gameplay.

[b]FINAL BOSS[/b]

I won’t lie, I plan to leave this as one of the last things to be added to the game, as my primary focus is on creating a fun/functional gameplay experience with the fewest bugs possible. The final boss implementation will likely be added along with story mode.

[b]UPDATE SCHEDULE[/b]

I am following a routine of publishing the changes made during the week every Friday/Saturday. In weeks when the game won’t be altered, there will be updates like this, with a proposal to inform about future content planned for the game.

This is all the news I can think of at the moment. It may seem like a small amount, but I assure you that many of the things that have been added to the game were carefully considered, suggested, and implemented based on feedback from friends and players. This means that this won’t necessarily be all the updates for the game, as everything is subject to change, most likely for a positive and even better outcome than those mentioned above.

notes.title: PATCH - 0.2.1
PATCH - 0.20
notes.content:
A bit delayed, but what matters is the delivery. I present to you version 0.2.0, which includes changes or additions to mechanics and information that have been missing since the game's launch. Below is everything that was added or fixed in this version. I [b]RECOMMEND[/b] taking a quick look at the things that interest you, as not everything is fully explained or intuitive in the game yet. Consider this update as part 1 (functionality), with part 2 (revision) coming in the next update with the necessary improvements.

[b]ACCESSORY EFFECTS[/b]

You have no idea how much I wanted to implement this. A unique effect has been created for each accessory, each with its own characteristic to allow combinations with all the cats and staves. I won’t reveal the effects here, as I want you to discover them on your own. If you already have accessories in your save, I recommend checking the game manual in the lobby for their updated descriptions, which now include their effects at the end.

This isn’t described anywhere yet, but some accessories have their [b]effects[/b] increased when upgraded. To avoid frustration for those with this functionality, I’ll list the ones that have this: [b]Chief's Hat, Cap, Beret, Top Hat, Clawdalf's Hat[/b]. In upcoming updates, I’ll add the effect description and its respective current and next upgrade values in the upgrade area.

[b]SHOP WITH MORE INFORMATION[/b]

I noticed a lot of feedback about the high prices of items and took that into consideration with this idea. To make your hard-earned money more valuable, I added a [b]description below the cats’ names[/b] so you can get an idea of each cat’s unique ability, even if you haven’t purchased them. Some descriptions might be a bit vague, but at least you’ll have a better understanding of what you’re buying, avoiding potential disappointment from blind purchases. I only added this to the cats because the menu layout wouldn’t allow for more changes without a complete shop menu overhaul.

[b]REROLL SYSTEM[/b]

Last but not least, [b]REROLL[/b]. You can now use Golden tokens dropped during the match to reroll those sad rolls with things you don’t want or need... for a price, of course. As a base, [b]the cost will be 1 Golden token for rerolls and 2 Golden tokens to increase the rarity of all cards.[/b] Note that the cost increases gradually with each use and resets to the base values at the start of the next wave. A certain [b]accessory[/b] can help out in this area, enhancing this newly implemented mechanic.
